note: Oxlint js-plugins is an opt-in preset; core and react are the defaults. ESLint core runs the syntactic rules; type-aware is opt-in. Biome's core preset leaves `recommended` on, so recommended rules it doesn't mention are enabled too. Nursery rules are never enabled by recommended.

classes.http-headers: HTTP security headers and server config (CWE-693, CWE-200)
classes.cross-origin: CORS, CSRF and postMessage (CWE-942, CWE-352, CWE-345)
classes.injection: SQL, OS command and template injection (CWE-89/78/1336)
classes.file-system: File permissions, uploads and temp dirs (CWE-732/434/377)
classes.data-exposure: Secrets or tokens exposed to the client

rules.detects: eval(…), (0, eval)(…), globalThis.eval, globalThis['eval'], Reflect.apply(eval); window.eval only with the browser env; not self.eval
setTimeout/setInterval/execScript with a string, template or same-file const string; Oxlint only when the browser env is set
new Function(…) and Function(…) by name; not aliases or Function.prototype.constructor
string literals that start with javascript: (not templates or split strings)

rules.description: Disallow the use of `eval()`-like functions
rules.detects: type-aware: implied eval, including setTimeout(string) through variables and new Function

rules.description: Disallow unsafe DOM HTML APIs.
rules.detects: writes to innerHTML/outerHTML/srcdoc (also el['innerHTML']), insertAdjacentHTML, createContextualFragment, setHTMLUnsafe, setAttribute('srcdoc'), document.write/writeln

rules.description: Disallow interpolation into SQL strings passed to Node’s `node:sqlite` APIs.
rules.detects: interpolation into SQL passed to node:sqlite

rules.description: Do not use `document.cookie` directly.
Enforce using the `targetOrigin` argument with `window.postMessage()`.
Disallow usage of dangerous JSX properties
rules.detects: the dangerouslySetInnerHTML JSX prop (Oxlint also createElement props; neither a spread object)

rules.description: Disallow when a DOM element is using both children and dangerouslySetInnerHTML
rules.detects: dangerouslySetInnerHTML together with children (a correctness check)

rules.description: Disallow `target="_blank"` attribute without `rel="noreferrer"`
rules.detects: target="_blank" (literal or conditional) on links to external or dynamic URLs without rel="noreferrer"; noopener alone is flagged, internal links and forms are not

rules.description: Disallow usage of `javascript:` URLs
rules.detects: a literal javascript: URL in a JSX href

rules.description: Enforce sandbox attribute on iframe elements
rules.detects: <iframe> without sandbox, or with a literal allow-scripts + allow-same-origin; Oxlint also document.createElement('iframe')

rules.description: disallow `Element.prototype.innerHTML` in favor of `Element.prototype.textContent`
disallow creating dynamic script tags
rules.detects: document.createElement('script'), whatever is assigned to it

rules.description: disallow usage of CSRF tokens in JavaScript
rules.detects: reading Rails authenticity_token (CSRF token) values in JavaScript

rules.description: disallow unescaped HTML literals
rules.detects: HTML string literals and templates that interpolate without escaping

rules.description: AWS API Gateway should require authentication
rules.detects: AWS CDK: API Gateway without auth

rules.description: Public network access to cloud resources should be disabled
EBS volumes should be encrypted
Amazon EFS file systems should be encrypted
Policies should not grant all privileges
IAM policies should not grant access to all account resources
AWS IAM policies should limit the scope of permissions given
AWS resource-based policies should not grant public access
OpenSearch domains should have encryption at rest enabled
Amazon RDS resources should be encrypted at rest
Administration services access should be restricted to specific IP addresses
rules.detects: AWS CDK: admin ports open to 0.0.0.0/0

rules.description: S3 buckets should not grant access to all users or authenticated users
S3 buckets should enforce HTTPS-only access
Amazon S3 bucket public access should be fully blocked
Amazon S3 buckets should have versioning enabled
SageMaker notebook instances should be encrypted at rest
Amazon SNS topics should be encrypted at rest
SQS queues should be encrypted
Dynamic code execution should not use user-controlled data
rules.detects: eval, Function (including a local alias) and node:vm called with a non-literal argument, and dynamic javascript: URLs

rules.description: HTTP request content length should be limited
Content security policy fetch directives should not be disabled
Cookies should have the "HttpOnly" flag
rules.detects: httpOnly: false passed to cookie-session, express-session, csurf or the cookies package (not Express res.cookie)

rules.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy should be restricted to trusted origins
rules.detects: cors() from the cors package, '*' set in an http.createServer callback, Express handlers reflecting the Origin header

rules.description: CSRF protections should not be disabled
rules.detects: csurf disabled or unsafe methods ignored

rules.description: Auto-escaping in HTML template engines should not be disabled
rules.detects: template engines with auto-escaping turned off

rules.description: Remote artifacts should not be used without integrity checks
rules.detects: type-aware: <script> created without an integrity attribute

rules.description: DOMPurify configuration should not be bypassable
Templates should not be constructed dynamically
rules.detects: server-side template engines compiling non-literal templates

rules.description: Encryption algorithms should be used with secure mode and padding scheme
File permissions should not be set to world-accessible values
rules.detects: x.chmod*/process.umask member calls with world-accessible modes (not named imports)

rules.description: File uploads should be restricted
Credentials should not be hard-coded
rules.detects: string literals matching known secret formats (keys, tokens)

rules.description: Weak hashing algorithms should not be used
rules.detects: MD5/SHA-1 and other weak hashes via crypto

rules.description: Cookies should have the "secure" flag
rules.detects: secure: false passed to the same cookie libraries as cookie-no-httponly

rules.description: JWT should be signed and verified with strong cipher algorithms
Opened windows should not have access to the originating page
rules.detects: window.open(url, '_blank') without noopener in the features

rules.description: Angular built-in sanitization should not be disabled
Clear-text protocols should not be used
rules.detects: http://, ftp://, telnet:// URLs (example.com and localhost excluded) and clear-text clients

rules.description: IP addresses should not be hardcoded
rules.detects: IP-address literals; loopback, unspecified and documentation addresses are excluded unless written as full-length IPv6

rules.description: Credentials should not be hard-coded
rules.detects: string literals (entropy ≥ 3 bits/char) under password-like names, and password= in literals

rules.description: Secrets should not be hard-coded
rules.detects: high-entropy string literals assigned to secret-like names

rules.description: Browsers should not be allowed to perform MIME type sniffing
OS commands should not rely on PATH resolution
HTTP Referrer-Policy should not be set to an unsafe value
rules.detects: helmet referrerPolicy set to an unsafe value

rules.description: Static Assets should not serve session cookies
Cipher algorithms should be robust
Cryptographic keys should be robust
Origins should be verified during cross-origin communications
rules.detects: type-aware: message listeners without origin checks

rules.description: Debugging features should not be enabled in production
Pseudorandom number generators (PRNGs) should not be used in security contexts
Temporary files should not be created in publicly writable directories
Wallet phrases should not be hard-coded
A new session should be created during user authentication
Regular expressions should not cause catastrophic backtracking
SQL queries should not be dynamically formatted
rules.detects: SQL built by concatenation or templates and passed to a known driver's query (pg, mysql, mysql2, sequelize, …)

rules.description: HTTP Strict-Transport-Security policy should not be disabled
rules.detects: helmet HSTS disabled or too short

rules.description: Regular expressions should not cause non-linear backtracking
Server certificates should be verified during SSL/TLS connections
Server hostnames should be verified during SSL/TLS connections
Weak SSL/TLS protocols should not be used
Web application technologies should not disclose version information
XML parsers should not be vulnerable to XXE attacks

rules.detects: BaaS authority map shipped in browser artifact
Server env leaked to browser artifact
Build pipeline runs code near secrets
Broad cookie or credentialed CORS trust
HTML injection sink with dynamic content
Firestore query filter used as authorization
Git provider URL built from interpolation
Raw HTML injection can run unsafe markup
Path containment check uses a string prefix
Plugin or updater trust boundary risk
Raw SQL built outside parameter binding
Unsanitized raw HTML in React Markdown
CSP nonce is not shared across server rendering
Request input spread without field allowlist
Hardcoded secret fallback for env var
Supabase table created without Row Level Security
Unescaped JSON in HTML or script sink
Server fetch follows redirects for caller-shaped URL

biome.detects: literal target="_blank" on links and forms (internal too) without rel noopener or noreferrer
the dangerouslySetInnerHTML prop, in JSX and createElement (not a spread object)
eval(…), aliases, window/globalThis.eval, Reflect.apply(eval); not self.eval or new Function
a literal javascript: URL in a JSX href (not other string literals)
high-entropy and known-format secrets in string literals
